newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts end lower as bond markets await Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts end lower as bond markets await Greenspan.

text.p: 1520 GMT - UK gilt futures ended lower after tracking international bond markets down ahead of testimony by Fed chairman Greenspan on Tuesday and Wednesday. Wednesday will also be a key day for UK, with June retail sales data and gilt auction. * Sept gilt contract ended 9/32 lower at 114-15/32.
"Greenspan is going to keep people nervous. We expect to see a little more profit-taking on Treasuries but we don't think Greenspan will say anything that is going to shock the market."
June retail sales data are expected to be strong, providing eagerly awaited evidence about the extent to which "windfall" gains from building society flotations are being spent.

Michael Saunders of Salomon Brothers expects retail sales to rise 0.4 percent on the month and 4.5 percent year-on-year in June, in line with the Reuters consensus forecast. He cites survey evidence, strong growth in narrow money supply and anecdotal evidence from retailers.

"We expect sales to continue to rise steadily on a month-on-month basis but the annual gain in sales will probably dip because of base effects from a big rise in spending a year ago," Saunders wrote in his Sterling Weekly.
Rayner sees good demand for Wednesday's auction stock given a general absence of new issues of long-dated paper in Europe. He expects cover of three times or more.

"There is fairly strong demand for long dated paper from the institutions. Pension funds and insurance companies seem to be fairly liquid. Surveys say they want to increase their bond weightings and there's not much paper around," he said.
The gilt-Bund spread at 10 years was 161 basis points compared with Friday's 158 close.
September short sterling was unchanged at 92.78, implying base rates of around 7.25 percent at the end of the third quarter compared with 6.75 percent at present.
